column1: # analysis/naming/ram_sdk.tsv - PROPOSED RAM names for the Mobile Adapter SDK block (agent naming_sdk); NOT applied to config/ram.
# Same columns as config/ram/*.tsv: addr name size type status evidence. A proposed row supersedes config/ram/sdk.tsv rows inside its range (several 1-byte rows are merged into words/arrays).

# Rows D000-D625 are in WRAM BANK 5 (the mail-library callers in bank 54 set SVBK=5): they collide by address with unrelated bank-1 names in config/ram/rom0_ram.tsv (wBank4*), so they must be applied as banked names or kept as documentation.

# Statuses: CONFIRMED = bytes/trace demonstrate it; PROBABLE = 2+ code evidences; HYPOTHESIS = weak. Crystal wMobileSDK_* names are imported from the community disassembly only where the code identity is proven (wMobileSDK_PacketChecksum, wMobileSDK_AdapterType, wMobileSDK_SendCommandID, ...Buffer names).

# Tested: with config/ram/sdk.tsv replaced by the C6xx-C9E4 rows below (minus C69F, whose byte is already wTimerEnable in rom0_ram.tsv) the ROM still rebuilds identically. C6C1 keeps rom0 name wMobileFlags (bits: 0 status poll in flight/alt rx buffer, 1 byte in flight, 3 resend pending, 4 data-transfer (connected) mode, 5 tx pending, 6 inside MobileAPI, 7 prepared data packet); C825 keeps wMobileAPIIndex.

# Adversarial re-check: the C6xx-C9E4 rows (minus C69F) were loaded as config/ram/sdk.tsv in a scratch config and `verify --strict` printed IDENTICAL; spot-checked roles (C6A8/C6AA/C6AB/C6AC/C6B2/C6B4 receive path, C6DD/C6F1 server names, C6D2 date pointer, C70F/C710 by adapter type) against the code. D002 in WRAM bank 5 is the mail selector although the generated source still shows the unrelated name wBank4SavedBankHi for it.

column6: evidence

SDK status flags (Crystal wc821): bit0 API busy (SetBusy 75:4437, tested by every API handler), bit1 event/error pending (SetErrorEvent 75:422A, cleared by PollResult 75:4115), bit2 more reply data pending, bit3 peer data pending, bit4 call active (RxDialReply 75:5D73 sets, RxHangUpReply 75:5BF3 clears), bits5-7 telephone-status class (75:5E26); Int_VBlank uses bit4/bit0 to gate the two comm-time clocks; same byte as rom0 name wTimerEnable (was wTimerEnable)
serial engine phase: 0 idle, 1 transmitting a packet (PacketSendBytes 75:5F14), 3 receiving (75:56D2); bit0/bit1 tested first by MobileSDK_SerialReceive 75:56D2 (was wRam_C6A0)
bytes left of the packet being clocked out (16-bit LE, decremented per byte at 75:56DD; set by PacketSendBytes 75:5F3F)
address of the next tx byte (MobileSDK_TxNextByte 75:5B2B reads it, advances it)
phase code saved by PacketSendBytes (75:5F55) before overwriting C6A7; restored by MobileSDK_RestorePhaseCode 75:5F01 and RxFinish 75:5D25

phase code passed in B to PacketSendBytes: 1 BeginSession pending, 2 ready, 3 after logout/close, 4 after TCP-open/DNS/login reply, 5 request in flight, 6 error latched, 8 abort/timeout wait, $0A unknown reply (75:5F4E, set by the RX reply handlers 75:5BC7-5D6E); meaning of each value HYPOTHESIS (was wRam_C6A7)
last two reply bytes of a sent packet: C6A8 = adapter ack (command^$80) or transport error $F0-$F2, C6A9 = adapter device id|$80 (SerialReceive 75:56F2)
receive byte index inside the current stage / magic-hunt index (75:5804, 75:58E5)
receive stage: 0 magic ($99,$66), 1 header, 2 data, 3 checksum+ack, 4 complete (dispatch 75:57F4, complete handler 75:5B4A)
received data length (low byte of header[3], stored at 75:5886)
first data byte of an adapter error packet = the command that failed; written by Mobile_GetErrorCode 75:5E61, only ever written
last SDK error code ($10 no adapter, $12/$13/$17 dial, $14 config, $15 retries, $20/$21 argument/busy, $22-$26 ISP/TCP/timeout, $30-$33 mail/HTTP); returned by MobileAPI_PollResult
extra error information returned in HL by PollResult: ack low nibble (75:57E1), server reply code (75:68D9); Pop3ReplyError 75:6A42 stores code, E, D at C6AF..C6B1
running 16-bit receive checksum, big-endian (75:58D3); compared with the received checksum in RxTrailerByte; Crystal name wMobileSDK_PacketChecksum
set to 1 when the received checksum differs (75:58BB); tested by TxAckRxPacket 75:5AC7 to answer $F1
response time-out: C6B5 lo / C6B6 hi 16-bit down counter (one step per timer tick), C6B7 repeat count ($20, $60 for dial/TCP/DNS, $0B poll, $03 idle) (75:5753, 75:5A51)
resend/retry counter (75:57C3 increments, limit B=10 or 3; 75:5AD5 counts checksum retries)
size of the last packet queued by PacketSendBytes (saved at 75:5F37 for resends)
data pointer of the last queued packet (75:5F2F), read by MobileSDK_ResendPacket 75:5A17 via ld hl,$C6BA
reload value of the response counters: C6BF = count hi, C6C0 = count lo, loaded by MobileAPI_SetTimer 75:40FF from the timing table
4 bytes copied from the ISP-login reply data (MobileSDK_RxIspLoginReply 75:5BDE)
caller buffer whose first 2 bytes receive the received length (Pop3Retr/Top 75:4A8C, RxCopyToDest end 75:4AF9)
current write pointer for reply data / config bytes (RxReadConfigReply 75:5BF9, RxDnsReply 75:5D2C, RxCopyToDest 75:5CED)
free space left at the destination pointer (reached as C6C8+2 by RxCopyToDest 75:5CCB and HttpReadBody 75:5049)
bytes delivered so far to the caller buffer; copied into the buffer length prefix at the end (75:4B30)
last 5 bytes of the reply text seen by MobileSDK_TrackReplyTail 75:6832; ends checked for CR LF (75:67FA) and CR LF . CR LF (75:680C)
pointer to the caller date buffer taken from the request struct (HttpGet 75:4E2F / HttpPost 75:5203); written through by MobileSDK_HttpHdrDate 75:7026
1 after the adapter config image was read and validated (75:7542); cleared by MobileSDK_ApiDispatch (75:4041) unless the API is $0C/$0E/$10
DNS server pair (config image C723 copied at 75:62CE, or the caller pair of API $3E at 75:43A9); appended to the ISP-login packet
NUL-terminated SMTP server name copied from config bytes 0x4A.. (MobileState_ConnectIsp 75:62CB copies $2C bytes to C708); passed to the DNS query by DnsAndTcpOpen service 0 (75:462C)
NUL-terminated POP3 server name (rest of the $2C-byte copy); DnsAndTcpOpen service 1 (75:4633)
SDK high-level state: 1 idle, 2 connected, 3 SMTP session, 4 POP3 session, 5 error, >= $0A dispatched through MobileSDK_StateTable (75:614F)
substep counter of the current state (incremented before each handler call, 75:617C)
TCP connection id from the Open-TCP reply (75:5BCA); placed in TransferData/Close-TCP packets
set to service index+1 when a TCP connection is open (75:64DC); cleared on close/loss
caller result buffer pointer (Init DE / per-API DE); C70D also holds the service index 0/1/2 or $FF during connect (dual use, 75:461C, 75:4F..)
offset into MobileSDK_TimingTable chosen from the adapter type (12 Blue, 9 Yellow, 6 Red); passed to SetTimer by every API handler; stored by MobileState_IdentifyAdapter 75:61F1
first data byte of the Dial packet by adapter type: 0 Blue, 2 Yellow, 1 Red/Green (75:6235); libmobile commands.c agrees
pointer to the caller request struct of HttpGet/HttpPost (saved at 75:4EF4); +0 body/date, +2 URL
request path length computed by MobileSDK_UrlMeasurePath 75:51FB (weak: only its store 75:51FB seen)
dual use: HTTP POST body pointer (HttpAddContentLength 75:7416 restores it), SMTP recipient-list pointer (75:47D6); saved/restored around requests (75:7420)
dual use: remaining POST body length (HttpSendBodyChunk 75:7444) / caller size arguments of API $04/$38
adapter config image ("MA" magic, checksum at C7DD/E) on the connect/export paths and $FA-byte reply/receive window otherwise (cleared by ClearWindow 75:653C); size 250 from that clear loop
state saved by MobileAPI_TelephoneStatus (75:555A) and restored by MobileState_TelephoneStatus (75:74A6)
HTTP response parse state: 0 not started, 1 header lines, 2 body (75:6F77, 75:719B)
HTTP status code in BCD: C828 = tens/units, C829 = hundreds (ParseReplyCode result stored at 75:6F9A); 3 in C829 with 1/2 in C828 = redirect
value of the "Gb-Status:" response header (75:704E)
5 ASCII digits of the POST body length (FormatContentLength 75:53CB); skipped zeros by HttpContentLengthLine 75:6706
Open-TCP retry counter (75:64B1 compares with 5, 75:64B1 increments); cleared on success
holds the request struct pointer at entry (75:4E1A) and later the Authorization / Gb-Auth-ID line (75:7080, AuthBuildResponse 75:7683 output); extent C852-C8CB by the next variable, not measured
rx buffer used for status-poll replies (RxStoreByte 75:5686), Crystal name
rx write index of the current packet (RxStoreByte 75:5671, reset by Mobile_ResetReceivePacketBuffer 75:402A)
receive packet buffer: header[4] data checksum[2] ack[2] without the magic bytes; +3 = length, +4 first data byte
transmit/build buffer for all packets; +0/+1 = final-state flags/state pair (SetFinalState 75:56B6, StopLink 75:569C)
WRAM BANK 5 (bank-54 callers write SVBK=5 before 00:0247): SRAM bank currently read by the mail parsers; incremented by Mail_NextSramPage 75-style wrappers (0F:4338)
WRAM bank 5: scratch copy of the output SRAM bank (0F:48BE wrappers, 0F:4EA8)
WRAM bank 5: selector in / result out of the mail library (00:0247, 00:0274, 0F:4250, 0F:4260)
WRAM bank 5: SRAM bank of the output stream (0F:4EA4, 0F:5025)
WRAM bank 5: output stream pointer (Mail_EmitCrLf 0F:4EA4 reads D006 then D007/8 through ld hl,$D006)
WRAM bank 5: free bytes left in the output area, decremented by each emitter (0F:49DD)
WRAM bank 5: pointer into the caller item list (Mail_FetchComposeItem 0F:4F3D)
WRAM bank 5: result of Mail_FindKeywordValue: bank, pointer (2), length (0F:4B2A)
WRAM bank 5: set to 1 when a header/message scan ended without the expected terminator (0F:4A6F, 0F:4AC4)
WRAM bank 5: composer/encoder phase, $FF error; also "header name already emitted" flag in Mail_EmitHeaderField (0F:4F5D)
WRAM bank 5: scratch text buffer (header values, unfolded text) D024-D623 by the distance to the next variable; users 0F:4C0F, 0F:50B7
WRAM bank 5: dual use: boundary length (0F:463B) / start of the scratch text at D624 (Mail_DecodeEncodedWords, Mail_EncodeHeaderWords)
WRAM bank 5: MIME boundary text (max $40) stored by Mail_ParseMultipartBoundary 0F:4624
